Within the review period, 245,257 patients were ever enrolled on anti-retroviral therapy. 150,191 (61.2%) remained on treatment, 10,960 (4.5%) were transferred out to other facilities, 6926 (2.8%) died, 2139 (0.9%) self-terminated treatment and 75,041 (30.6%) had a loss to follow-up event captured

. Males (OR: 1.16), Non-pregnant female (OR: 4.55), Patients on ≥ 3-monthly ARV refills (OR: 1.32), Patients with un-suppressed viral loads on ART (OR: 4.52), patients on adult 2nd line regimen (OR: 1.23) or pediatric on 1st line regimen (OR: 1.70) were significantly more likely to be lost to follow-up. Despite increasing access to anti-retroviral therapy, loss to follow-up is still a challenge in the HIV program in Nigeria. Differentiated care approaches that will focus on males, non-pregnant females and paediatrics is encouraged. Reducing months of Anti-retroviral drug refill to less than 3 months is advocated for increased patient adherence.
Title: Clinical factors and outcomes associated with immune non-response among virally suppressed adults with HIV from Africa and the United States.

Abstract: A significant minority of people living with HIV (PLWH) achieve viral suppression (VS) on antiretroviral therapy (ART) but do not regain healthy CD4 counts. Clinical factors affecting this immune non-response (INR) and its effect on incident serious non-AIDS events (SNAEs) have been challenging to understand due to confounders that are difficult to control in many study settings. The U.S. Military HIV Natural History Study (NHS) and African Cohort Study (AFRICOS). PLWH with sustained VS (< 400 copies/ml for at least two years) were evaluated for INR (CD4 < 350 cells/µl at the time of sustained VS)

. Logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for factors associated with INR. Cox proportional hazards regression produced adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for factors associated with incident SNAE after sustained VS. INR prevalence was 10.8% and 25.8% in NHS and AFRICOS, respectively. Higher CD4 nadir was associated with decreased odds of INR (aOR = 0.34 [95% CI 0.29, 0.40] and aOR = 0.48 [95% CI 0.40, 0.57] per 100 cells/µl in NHS and AFRICOS, respectively). After adjustment, INR was associated with a 61% increase in relative risk of SNAE [95% CI 1.12, 2.33]

. Probability of "SNAE-free" survival at 15 years since sustained VS was approximately 20% lower comparing those with and without INR; nearly equal to the differences observed by 15-year age groups. CD4 monitoring before and after VS is achieved can help identify PLWH at risk for INR. INR may be a useful clinical indicator of future risk for SNAEs.
Title: Virological response and HIV drug resistance 12 months after antiretroviral therapy initiation at 2 clinics in Nigeria.

Abstract: This report describes a pilot study, conducted in Nigeria, of the World Health Organization protocol for monitoring human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) drug resistance (HIVDR) and associated program factors among patients receiving first-line antiretroviral therapy (ART). In 2008, 283 HIV-infected patients starting ART were consecutively enrolled at 2 ART clinics in Abuja. Twelve months after ART initiation, 62% were alive and on first-line ART, 3% had died, 1% had transferred out of the program, and 34% were lost to follow-up. Among patients on first-line ART at 12 months, 90% had viral suppression

. Among patients on first-line ART at 12 months, 90% had viral suppression. However, in view of the high loss to follow-up rate (34%), strategies for patient retention and tracking are critical to minimize possible HIVDR and optimize treatment outcomes.
Title: Immuno-virologic outcomes and immuno-virologic discordance among adults alive and on anti-retroviral therapy at 12 months in Nigeria.

Abstract: Predictors of immuno-virologic outcomes and discordance and their associations with clinical, demographic, socio-economic and behavioral risk factors are not well described in Nigeria since HIV viral load testing is not routinely offered in public HIV treatment programs. The HACART study was a multi-center observational clinic-based cohort study of 2585 adults who started HAART between April 2008 and February 2009. A total of 628 patients were randomly selected at 12 months for immuno-virologic analyses. Virologic suppression rate (<400 copies/ml) was 76.7%, immunologic recovery rate (CD4 change from baseline ≥50 cells/mm3) was 77.4% and immuno-virologic discordance rate was 33%

. In multivariate logistic regression, virologic failure was associated with age <30 years (OR 1.79; 95% CI: 1.17-2.67, p=0.03), anemia (Hemoglobin < 10 g/dl) (OR 1.71; 95% CI: 1.22-2.61, p=0.03), poor adherence (OR 3.82; 95% CI: 2.17-5.97, p=0.001), and post-secondary education (OR 0.60; 95% CI: 0.30-0.86, p=0.02). Immunologic failure was associated with male gender (OR 1.46; 95% CI: 1.04-2.45, p=0.04), and age <30 years (OR 1.50; 95% CI: 1.11-2.39, p=0.03)

. Virologic failure with immunologic success (VL-/CD4+) was associated with anemia (OR 1.80; 95% CI: 1.13-2.88, p=0.03), poor adherence (OR 3.90; 95% CI: 1.92-8.24, p=0.001), and post-secondary education (OR 0.40; 95% CI: 0.22-0.68, p=0.005). Although favorable immuno-virologic outcomes could be achieved in this large ART program, immuno-virologic discordance was observed in a third of the patients. Focusing on intensified treatment preparation and adherence, young patients, males, persons with low educational status and most importantly baseline anemia assessment and management may help address predictors of poor immuno-virologic outcomes, and improve overall HIV program impact
. Viral load testing in addition to the CD4 testing should be considered to identify, characterize and address negative immuno-virologic outcomes and discordance.

Guideline: WHO Global HIV Treatment Guidelines
Section: WHO Recommended First-Line ART Regimens

WHO 2021 Consolidated Guidelines on HIV — Recommended First-Line ART:

Preferred first-line regimen for adults and adolescents:
- Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300mg + Lamivudine 300mg + Dolutegravir 50mg (TDF/3TC/DTG) — ONE tablet once daily
- This is the preferred regimen globally including all low and middle income countries
- Replaces the previous standard of TDF/3TC/EFV as first-line

Why TDF/3TC/DTG is WHO preferred:
- Dolutegravir has a higher barrier to resistance than efavirenz
- Superior viral suppression rates compared to efavirenz-based regimens
- Better tolerability with fewer CNS side effects than efavirenz
- Once daily single pill improves adherence
- Fixed-dose combination available as a single tablet
- Lower cost than TAF-based regimens used in high-income countries

Alternative first-line regimens:
- TDF/3TC/EFV 400mg — low-dose efavirenz, acceptable alternative
- TDF/3TC/EFV 600mg — standard dose efavirenz still widely used
- ABC/3TC/DTG — for patients with renal impairment where TDF is contraindicated

Guideline: Nigeria HIV Treatment Guidelines
Section: Nigeria National ART Guidelines First-Line Regimens

Nigeria National HIV/AIDS Treatment Guidelines — First-Line ART:

Recommended first-line regimen in Nigeria:
- TDF + 3TC + DTG (Tenofovir/Lamivudine/Dolutegravir) — preferred first-line for all treatment-naive adults
- Available as fixed-dose combination — one tablet once daily
- Dispensed through PEPFAR-supported ART sites including APIN, IHVN, CCCRN

Previous standard now used as alternative:
- TDF/3TC/EFV 600mg — was first-line before DTG scale-up, still used in some settings

metadata.source: Nigeria FMOH: National HIV/AIDS Treatment Guidelines
metadata.section: Nigeria National ART Guidelines First-Line Regimens

text:
Special populations:
- Pregnant women: TDF/3TC/DTG recommended throughout pregnancy including first trimester
- TB/HIV coinfection: TDF/3TC/EFV preferred when on rifampicin. DTG dose doubled to 50mg twice daily if DTG used with rifampicin
- Renal impairment eGFR below 50: switch TDF to ABC — use ABC/3TC/DTG

Second-line ART:
- After TDF/3TC/DTG failure: AZT/3TC + boosted PI (lopinavir/ritonavir or atazanavir/ritonavir)

Context:
- Nigeria has approximately 1.9 million PLHIV
- PEPFAR supports approximately 90 percent of patients on ART in Nigeria
- DTG-based regimens scaled up nationally from 2020

text:
Guideline: Adult & Adolescent ARV Treatment
Section: First-Line ART Regimens Detailed

DHHS Recommended First-Line ART Regimens for Treatment-Naive Adults:

Preferred Regimens:
1. Bictegravir 50mg + Tenofovir alafenamide 25mg + Emtricitabine 200mg (BIC/TAF/FTC) — Biktarvy. One pill once daily.
2. Dolutegravir 50mg + Tenofovir alafenamide 25mg + Emtricitabine 200mg (DTG + TAF/FTC). Once daily.
3. Dolutegravir 50mg + Lamivudine 300mg (DTG/3TC) — Dovato. Two-drug regimen only for patients with HIV RNA below 500,000 copies per mL and no HBV coinfection.

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: DHHS Adult & Adolescent ARV Guidelines

text:
Alternative Regimens:
1. Darunavir/Cobicistat/TAF/FTC — when INSTI resistance is suspected
2. Raltegravir 400mg twice daily + TDF/FTC
3. Efavirenz 600mg + TDF/FTC — useful in TB coinfection on rifampicin

Note: DHHS prefers TAF over TDF due to better renal and bone profile. WHO prefers TDF globally due to lower cost. Both are clinically effective.

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: DHHS Adult & Adolescent ARV Guidelines

text:
Guideline: Adult & Adolescent ARV Treatment
Section: When to Start ART

ART is recommended for all individuals with HIV regardless of CD4 count. Early initiation reduces AIDS-defining events, non-AIDS morbidity, and HIV transmission.

Rapid ART initiation on the same day or within days of diagnosis is recommended for most patients. Evidence from HPTN 052 and START trials confirmed that early ART significantly reduces both AIDS and serious non-AIDS events.

Exceptions where initiation may be deferred:
- Active cryptococcal meningitis: defer 4 to 6 weeks to avoid IRIS
- Active TB meningitis: defer 8 weeks
- Need for patient education and treatment readiness assessment

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: DHHS Adult & Adolescent ARV Guidelines

text:
Guideline: Adult & Adolescent ARV Treatment
Section: Drug Interactions Rifampicin and ARVs

Rifampicin is a potent inducer of CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein and significantly reduces plasma concentrations of many ARVs.

Key interactions:
- Rifampicin reduces dolutegravir AUC by approximately 54 percent. Dolutegravir dose should be increased to 50mg twice daily.
- Rifampicin reduces efavirenz levels modestly. Standard 600mg dose is generally maintained.
- Rifampicin is contraindicated with most protease inhibitors and cobicistat-boosted regimens.
- Rifabutin is preferred over rifampicin when a PI-based regimen is required.

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: DHHS Adult & Adolescent ARV Guidelines

text:
For HIV/TB coinfected patients on rifampicin:
- Preferred: efavirenz-based regimen TDF/3TC/EFV
- Alternative: dolutegravir 50mg twice daily plus TDF/3TC

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: DHHS Adult & Adolescent ARV Guidelines

text:
Guideline: Adult & Adolescent ARV Treatment
Section: Switching and Simplifying ART Regimens

Virologically suppressed patients may switch ART for toxicity, drug interactions, pill burden, or cost.

Key considerations:
- Confirm viral suppression before switching
- Review resistance history as prior resistance may limit options
- TAF-based regimens preferred over TDF in renal impairment or osteoporosis per DHHS
- TDF remains preferred in WHO and Nigerian guidelines due to cost
- DTG/3TC is effective 2-drug maintenance for stable patients without HBV or prior NRTI resistance

TANGO trial: DTG/3TC was non-inferior to TAF-based 3-drug regimens through 144 weeks.

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: DHHS Adult & Adolescent ARV Guidelines

text:
Guideline: Adult & Adolescent ARV Treatment
Section: HIV and Renal Disease

HIV-associated nephropathy and TDF-related nephrotoxicity are key renal considerations.

TDF can cause proximal tubular dysfunction and reduced GFR. TAF achieves higher intracellular concentrations at lower plasma levels with significantly less renal and bone toxicity.

Recommendations:
- DHHS: Use TAF-based regimens if eGFR below 60 mL per min
- WHO/Nigeria: Switch from TDF to ABC if eGFR below 50 mL per min
- Monitor renal function every 6 months on TDF
- Avoid TDF if eGFR below 30 mL per min
- Screen for HIVAN with urine protein to creatinine ratio at baseline and annually

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: DHHS Adult & Adolescent ARV Guidelines

text:
Guideline: Adult & Adolescent ARV Treatment
Section: HIV Drug Resistance Testing

Resistance testing is recommended at HIV diagnosis and before initiating or changing ART.

Types:
- Genotypic testing sequences RT, protease, and integrase genes. Faster and cheaper.
- Phenotypic testing directly measures viral replication in drug. Used for complex resistance.

Indications:
- All patients at entry into care
- Before ART initiation in treatment-naive patients
- Virologic failure defined as HIV RNA above 200 copies per mL on ART

Key mutations: M184V confers 3TC/FTC resistance, K65R confers TDF resistance, Q148H/R/K confers INSTI resistance, K103N confers NNRTI resistance.

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: DHHS Adult & Adolescent ARV Guidelines

text:
Guideline: Long-Acting Injectable ART
Section: Cabotegravir and Rilpivirine Long-Acting Injectable

Long-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine known as CAB+RPV LA or Cabenuva is approved for virologically stable adults.

ATLAS and FLAIR trial data:
- CAB+RPV LA every 2 months was non-inferior to daily oral ART
- 94 percent of participants preferred injectable over daily oral therapy
- Injection site reaction discontinuation rate was approximately 2 percent

Eligibility:
- Virologically suppressed with HIV RNA below 50 copies per mL
- No history of treatment failure
- No resistance to cabotegravir or rilpivirine
- No HBV coinfection

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: DHHS Adult & Adolescent ARV Guidelines

text:
ATLAS-2M confirmed every-2-month dosing is non-inferior to monthly dosing.

Note: Currently limited availability in Nigeria and most African settings due to cost.

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: DHHS Adult & Adolescent ARV Guidelines

text:
Guideline: PrEP Guidelines
Section: PrEP Efficacy and Indications

Pre-exposure prophylaxis with TDF/FTC or TAF/FTC is highly effective in preventing HIV acquisition.

Key trials:
- iPrEx: TDF/FTC reduced HIV incidence by 44 percent overall and more than 90 percent with detectable drug levels
- Partners PrEP: 75 percent efficacy in serodiscordant heterosexual couples
- DISCOVER: TAF/FTC non-inferior to TDF/FTC in MSM and transgender women
- PURPOSE 1 and PURPOSE 2: near-complete protection in cisgender women

Indications include adults and adolescents at substantial HIV risk, serodiscordant couples, MSM with inconsistent condom use or recent STI, and people who inject drugs.
Adherence is the strongest predictor of PrEP efficacy.

Guideline: PrEP Guidelines
Section: PrEP in Special Populations

PrEP uptake varies significantly across populations due to structural and social barriers.

Black and Latino MSM:
- High HIV incidence but lower PrEP uptake than white MSM
- Barriers include medical mistrust, insurance gaps, stigma, and provider bias

Transgender women:
- TAF/FTC preferred due to absence of interaction with feminizing hormones

People who inject drugs:
- TDF/FTC reduces HIV incidence
- Integrated harm reduction and PrEP programs improve retention

Adolescents:
- FDA-approved for adolescents weighing at least 35kg
- School-based and youth-friendly clinics improve adherence

Nigeria and sub-Saharan Africa:
- PrEP scale-up ongoing through PEPFAR supported programs
- TDF/FTC used as PrEP in Nigeria — TAF not widely available

Guideline: HIV in Pregnancy
Section: ART in Pregnancy Recommendations

All pregnant people with HIV should receive ART regardless of CD4 count or viral load for health and PMTCT.

Preferred regimens in pregnancy:
- WHO and Nigeria FMOH: TDF/3TC/DTG preferred throughout pregnancy including first trimester
- DHHS: DTG-based regimens preferred. Neural tube defect risk low at approximately 0.1 percent.
- Raltegravir plus TDF/FTC remains an alternative
- Efavirenz-based regimens acceptable if started before conception

Goals:
- Achieve viral suppression below 200 copies per mL before delivery
- Undetectable viral load reduces perinatal transmission to below 1 percent
- Cesarean delivery recommended if viral load exceeds 1000 copies per mL near delivery

Guideline: Opportunistic Infection Prevention
Section: PCP and Toxoplasmosis Prophylaxis

PCP prophylaxis is indicated for CD4 below 200 cells per mm3, CD4 percentage below 14 percent, or prior PCP episode.

Preferred: TMP-SMX one double-strength tablet daily.
Alternatives for sulfa-allergic patients: Dapsone, atovaquone, or aerosolized pentamidine.

Toxoplasma prophylaxis:
- Indicated for Toxoplasma IgG-positive patients with CD4 below 100 cells per mm3
- TMP-SMX DS daily also covers Toxoplasma
- Discontinue when CD4 exceeds 200 cells per mm3 for more than 3 months on ART

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: Guidelines for Prevention of Opportunistic Infections

text:
Guideline: Opportunistic Infection Prevention
Section: Cryptococcal Meningitis Management

Cryptococcus neoformans meningitis is a leading cause of mortality in HIV with CD4 below 100 cells per mm3.

Prevention:
- CrAg screening for CD4 below 100 cells per mm3 in high-prevalence settings including Nigeria
- Fluconazole pre-emptive therapy for CrAg-positive patients

Treatment:
- Induction: Liposomal amphotericin B plus flucytosine for 2 weeks
- Consolidation: Fluconazole 400mg daily for 8 weeks
- Maintenance: Fluconazole 200mg daily until CD4 exceeds 200 for more than 1 year on ART

Defer ART 4 to 6 weeks after antifungal initiation to reduce IRIS risk.

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: Guidelines for Prevention of Opportunistic Infections

text:
Guideline: Opportunistic Infection Prevention
Section: CMV and MAC Prophylaxis

MAC prophylaxis:
- Indicated for CD4 below 50 cells per mm3
- Preferred: Azithromycin 1200mg weekly
- Discontinue when CD4 exceeds 100 cells per mm3 for more than 3 months on ART

CMV:
- Routine prophylaxis not recommended
- CMV retinitis screening for CD4 below 50 cells per mm3
- Treatment: IV ganciclovir or oral valganciclovir
- Secondary prophylaxis until CD4 exceeds 100 to 150 cells per mm3

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: Guidelines for Prevention of Opportunistic Infections

text:
Guideline: HIV TB Coinfection
Section: TB Treatment in HIV-Positive Patients

TB is the leading cause of death among HIV-positive individuals globally and particularly in Nigeria.

ART timing:
- CD4 below 50 cells per mm3: start ART within 2 weeks of TB treatment
- CD4 at or above 50: start ART within 8 weeks
- TB meningitis: defer ART 8 weeks regardless of CD4

Preferred ART with rifampicin in Nigeria:
- TDF/3TC/EFV 600mg — efavirenz not significantly affected by rifampicin
- Alternative: TDF/3TC + DTG 50mg twice daily — dose doubled due to rifampicin induction

IRIS management: NSAIDs or corticosteroids for severe cases. Continue both ART and TB treatment.

metadata.source: Nigeria FMOH: National HIV/AIDS Treatment Guidelines TB Coinfection

text:
Guideline: HIV and Mental Health
Section: Depression Adherence and Mental Health in HIV

Mental health comorbidities are highly prevalent in PLHIV and directly impact ART adherence.

Prevalence:
- Depression affects 30 to 40 percent of PLHIV compared to approximately 7 percent in general population
- Anxiety, PTSD, and substance use disorders are also elevated

Impact:
- Depression is one of the strongest predictors of ART non-adherence
- Untreated depression linked to faster disease progression and higher mortality

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: DHHS Adult & Adolescent ARV Guidelines
metadata.section: Depression Adherence and Mental Health in HIV

text:
Management:
- Screen with PHQ-9 at entry to care and annually
- SSRIs are first-line. Check ARV drug interactions.
- Efavirenz associated with neuropsychiatric side effects. Consider switching.
- Integrated HIV and mental health care improves adherence and psychiatric outcomes

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: DHHS Adult & Adolescent ARV Guidelines
metadata.section: Depression Adherence and Mental Health in HIV

text:
Guideline: HIV Prevention
Section: Treatment as Prevention and Undetectable Equals Untransmittable

Treatment as prevention is a cornerstone of HIV prevention globally.

Evidence:
- PARTNER, PARTNER2, and Opposites Attract studies observed zero linked transmissions from virologically suppressed individuals
- Applies to heterosexual and MSM serodiscordant couples
- Requires sustained viral suppression below 200 copies per mL

HPTN 052: early ART reduced transmission to partners by 96 percent.

metadata.source: AIDSinfo: DHHS Adult & Adolescent ARV Guidelines
metadata.section: Treatment as Prevention and Undetectable Equals Untransmittable

text:
HPTN 052: early ART reduced transmission to partners by 96 percent.

Public health implications:
- UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets: 95 percent diagnosed, 95 percent on ART, 95 percent virally suppressed
- Nigeria 95-95-95 progress: significant gaps remain particularly in the second and third 95
- Test and treat combined with PrEP provides the most effective combination prevention
